definition.body: Implicit memory is the human-made cognitive category for memory systems that operate without conscious awareness, intentional recall, or deliberate retrieval. Parameters: (1) content — information stored and expressed through performance rather than conscious recollection, including motor skills, perceptual priming, classical conditioning, and non-associative learning; (2) expression — the stored influence manifests as improved performance, faster response times, or altered behavior without the subject's awareness of the source; (3) consciousness boundary — unlike declarative memory, implicit memory does not require or produce conscious access to the encoded content, though awareness of the task being performed may be present. It persists as a maintained classification in cognitive psychology textbooks, experimental paradigms (word-fragment completion, priming tasks, skin-conductance conditioning), and clinical neuropsychology for dissociating amnesic from intact memory systems. e.g.: the word-fragment priming paradigm in cognitive psychology experiments; motor skill retention in patients with hippocampal amnesia per the Mirror Drawing Task study by Squire and Zola-Morgan; classical conditioning of eye-blink response in Clark, Squire, and Steriade; the distinction between implicit and explicit memory in Schacter and Wagner's annual review of psychology | not: declarative-memory (conscious, intentionally retrievable memory); episodic-memory (conscious recall of personal events; a subtype of declarative not implicit) [formal: memoria implicita | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

definition.body: Inverse Short-Time Fourier Transform (ISTFT) is a signal-processing algorithm that reconstructs a time-domain signal from its short-time Fourier transform representation. Parameters: (1) window type — the analysis window function originally applied during STFT; (2) window size — the segment length in samples matching the original STFT; (3) hop size — the step between consecutive STFT frames; (4) window overlap — how consecutive segments are combined via overlap-add. The algorithm computes the inverse DFT of each frequency-bin segment, applies the inverse of the analysis window, and sums overlapping segments. definition.body: A gabor transform is a time-frequency analysis method that applies a sliding Gaussian window to a signal, computing the Fourier transform within each window position to produce a joint time-frequency representation. Unlike the generic STFT which permits arbitrary windows, the Gabor transform uses a symmetric Gaussian window function, which minimizes the Heisenberg-Gabor uncertainty product and yields the sharpest possible joint localization in time and frequency. Parameters: (1) the window width sigma, which sets the trade-off between time and frequency resolution; (2) the sampling grid in the time-frequency plane, specified as a time step and frequency step; (3) the window position sequence, which may be uniformly spaced or non-uniform.
